title: Bioluminescent optogenetic (BL-OG) activation of neurons during mouse postnatal brain development
protocol: Reconstitute water-soluble CTZ or vehicle by adding 500 μL sterile water to a vial containing 500 μg of powder.
Incubate the reconstituted solution in a 55°C water bath for a few minutes until completely dissolved.
Transfer the dissolved solution into a black microcentrifuge tube.
Rinse the glass vial walls with additional solution to retrieve all CTZ or vehicle.
Remove the amount of solution needed for injection with a 0.5 mL insulin syringe.
Store leftover solution at 4°C for use the next day, discarding after 24 hours.
Inject postnatal pups as required by experimental design.
Pull up CTZ or vehicle solution into 0.5 mL insulin syringe with a 31 gauge needle as needed for injecting a litter.
Remove any bubbles from the syringe containing CTZ or vehicle solution.
Cover the syringe containing CTZ in aluminum foil when transporting to the animal facility.
Inject pups intraperitoneally (ip) with volumes specified in step 2a.
Use separate syringes if more than one litter is being injected.
Inject pups aged postnatal days 1 to 5 in a lower quadrant.
Take out the entire litter for injection.
Inject pups in a lower quadrant.
Draw plunger back before expelling the desired volume into the body cavity.
Return injected neonates as a group to minimize disturbing the dam.
Prepare CTZ or vehicle solution and inject pups immediately before imaging.
Follow manufacturer’s protocols using Living Image Software for bioluminescent imaging.
Take images in 5-min bins over a 20- to 30-min period.
Anesthetize neonates up to 5 days old by hypothermia during imaging.
Inject CTZ ip in anesthetized pups.
Place pups on crushed ice in a dish after injection.
Transfer dish with pups into IVIS chamber as soon as pups stop moving for imaging.
Keep pups on heating pad until pink and moving after imaging is completed.
Anesthetize neonates older than 5 days old using isoflurane anesthesia (oxygen 2 L/min; isoflurane 1–2%).
Inject CTZ ip in anesthetized older pups.
Place pups in induction chamber for isoflurane anesthesia and collect images in 5-min bins.
Make the patch rig light tight.
Create a light tight compartment around the recording rig using black drapes.
Provide access by keeping the flexible black drape in the front rolled-up.
Drop the front drape at the time of CTZ treatment and bioluminescence imaging while recording from the patched cell.
Cover all light sources present inside the light tight compartment, such as LED indicators on the camera.
Prepare CTZ stocks.
Reconstitute lyophilized CTZ in 25 μL of NanoFuel Solvent.
Dissolve all CTZ along the walls of the vial by pipetting or vortexing.
Prepare 5 μL aliquots in 0.5 mL black microcentrifuge tubes.
Store CTZ aliquots at −80°C for future use.
Anaesthetize the mouse pup via isoflurane inhalation.
Remove the head with sharp scissors.
Isolate the brain immediately and place it in ice-cold PRC buffer bubbled with carbogen gas.
Prepare 300 μm thick slices from the desired brain region using a Vibratome and ice-cold PRC buffer continuously bubbled with Carbogen.
Prepare brain slices from neonatal pups for recording.
Mount the slice into the recording chamber using a vibratome platform.
Store the slices in PRH buffer at 25°C for 1 h recovery before transferring to the recording chamber.
Transfer a brain slice to the recording chamber perfused with carbogenated ACSF (perfusion rate: 3 mL/min).
Set the heater temperature for the buffer inlet at 39°C to maintain the buffer temperature in the recording chamber around 35°C.
Place a C-shaped mesh harp over the slice to fix its position.
Identify a fluorescent cell under 480 nm excitation light using an established set-up (e.g., Multiclamp 700b amplifier and Digidata 1440 digitizer together with pClamp recording software).
Perform patch clamp recordings from LMO expressing cells.
Stimulate the patched LMO expressing cell with light of the appropriate wavelength from a physical source by delivering light through the objective or from a separate LED source.

Maintain membrane potential at −70 mV by continuously injecting negative DC current, less than 100 pA, in current clamp mode while delivering periodic square current injections to evoke firing (e.g., 0.1 Hz, 300 pA, 50 ms).
Bath apply CTZ and record from the patched LMO expressing cell.
Bath application of CTZ is expected to depolarize the membrane potential and increase the firing response to current stimulation.
Transfer 250 μL of carbogenated ACSF from the beaker into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 5 μL of 50 mM CTZ to the ACSF in the microcentrifuge tube and mix well.
Take out the inlet tube of the pump from the ACSF beaker.
Immerse the inlet tube quickly into the CTZ solution.
Remove the outlet tubing of the pump from the ACSF beaker.
Place the outlet tubing into a separate 50 mL tube to collect used reagent.
Dip the outlet tubing back into the ACSF beaker after the reagent has exited.
Turn off all lights in the room.
Observe bioluminescence in the recording chamber upon entry of CTZ.
Turn off all lights in the room for bioluminescence imaging setup.
Roll down the front black drape to make the patch rig completely light-tight if measurement of photon counts is desired.
Maintain ACSF bubbled with Carbogen at all times to preserve cell viability.
Construct a re-usable head mount for the neonatal skull to be fixed to the stereotaxic frame using ‘Gorilla Epoxy Putty Stick’.
Assemble all components needed (drill with small drill bit, electrode, LED optical cable and source, saline).
Turn on the warming pad and maintain at 37°C until the end of the recording session.
Anesthetize the pup.
Transfer the pup to a holding box padded with soft tissue.
Cover the pup with gauze to keep it warm.
Weigh the pup.
Calculate the amount of Urethane stock to be injected (1.0 g/kg).
Dilute the calculated volume of Urethane stock 1:2 with saline if less than 100 μL.
Inject the diluted or undiluted Urethane intraperitoneally into the abdomen.
Note the time of primary Urethane injection.
Return the pup to the warm and darkened holding box until it is anesthetized.
Boost anesthesia by acute application of Isoflurane if necessary.
Place a small gauze pad into a 10 mL plastic tube with a screw cap.
Add 1-2 drops of Isoflurane to the gauze in the tube and close lid.
Open the lid of the tube and hold it near the pup’s snout for 3 s before making an incision.
Fix the head mount to the pup's head.
Remove the skin from the head using scissors to expose the skull.
Dry the surface of the skull with Q-tips.
Apply Vet bond to glue the skin back onto the skull.
Fix the pre-constructed head mount to the prepared skull using C&B METABOND.
Take out a pre-chilled porcelain tray from −20°C freezer.
Mix the METABOND components quickly according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Align the head mount over the skull, ensuring Bregma is visible in the center and landmarks are clearly visualized through the window of the molded mount.
Apply the METABOND mixture along the circumference of the head mount and across the skull to fix it firmly to the skull.
Hold the pup gently while the METABOND solidifies for about 2–3 minutes.
Attach the head-mounted pup to ear bars by super gluing them to the two metal washers on the head mount.
Allow the glue to bond for at least the recommended time (1–2 min).
Place the pup into the stereotaxic frame via the attached ear bars.
Cover the pup from neck to tail with a soft cloth or gauze to keep it warm.
Perform a craniotomy on the pup using a surgical stereomicroscope.
Administer an additional dose of Urethane, which is 20% of the initial dose, to the pup.
Attach the optrode to the Omnetics holder and position it directly above the Bregma mark.
Adjust the digital stereotaxic apparatus for anterior/posterior (AP) and medial/lateral (ML) coordinates.
Move the electrode to the specified AP and ML coordinates and mark the location with a thin sharpie.
Lift the optrode holder and move it back to protect the electrode during craniotomy.
Use a hand-held, battery-operated drill to carefully create an opening in the skull without causing bleeding.
Drip saline onto the hole in the skull to prevent drying and ensure clear visibility of the brain surface.
Drill through any dried METABOND on the skull surface completely before proceeding with the mouse skull.
Confirm successful craniotomy by visual inspection and gently touching the surface with fine blunt forceps.
Drill a second hole over the cerebellum.
Using the X/Y/Z axis micromanipulators of the stereotaxic instrument, bring back the optrode to the front and align it carefully over the craniotomy of the target area.
Insert the silver wire connected to the optrode’s ground and reference ports through the second craniotomy into the cerebellum by hand.
Move the optrode down until the tip touches the brain surface.
Reset the dorsal/ventral (DV) values on the digital stereotaxic apparatus.
Record from the desired brain region of the pup.
Turn on the ephys set-up and software.
Slowly move the optrode tip dorso-ventrally in 10 micron steps using the micromanipulator.
Follow the progression of the probe into the brain according to the channel map for the optrode used.
Go down slowly while observing neural activity on the computer screen for each optrode channel.
Wait until consistent neural activity is observed in most channels at the desired depth within the brain.
Let neurons recover for about 30 min after achieving consistent neural activity.
Prepare water-soluble CTZ/vehicle solution during the neuron recovery phase.
Start recording baseline data for approximately 20 minutes before administering CTZ/vehicle injection.
Deliver a pulse of blue light via the optrode to check LMO-expressing neuron activity.
Lift the pup gently by its tail without disturbing the upper body.
Inject CTZ/vehicle intraperitoneally using an insulin syringe.
Place the pup back in its original position.
Record pup activity for the desired period.
Carefully remove the optrode from the brain immediately after recording.
Dip-clean the optrode with distilled water to avoid debris drying.
Clean the optrode further with Tergazyme or another suitable electrode cleaning reagent.
Remove the head mount and rig from the pup.
Surgically remove the pup’s brain.
Place the brain in fixative (4% PFA) for later histology if desired.
Dilute Urethane solution 1:2 to ensure injectable volume is ≤ 100 μL.
Inject diluted Urethane solution intraperitoneally for anesthesia.
Administer a booster dose of 20% of the original Urethane dose if necessary.
Deliver additional booster doses (20% of the original) 20–30 minutes apart if required.
